You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2020 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 27 [20 marks]: Evaluate human resource strategies used to achieve THREE indicators of effective human resource management.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 20):
17–20 marks: Makes a judgement about the human resource strategies used to achieve three indicators of effective human resource management | Applies relevant case study/studies and contemporary business issues | Presents a sustained, logical and cohesive response and communicates clearly using relevant business terminology and concepts
13–16 marks: Makes evident the relationship between human resource strategies and three indicators of effective human resource management | Uses relevant case study/studies and contemporary business issues | Presents a logical and cohesive response using relevant business terminology and concepts
9–12 marks: Provides characteristics and features of human resource strategies and three indicators of effective human resource management | Makes reference to case study/studies and/or contemporary business issues | Communicates using relevant business terminology and concepts
5–8 marks: Sketches in general terms human resource strategies and/or effective human resource management | May make reference to case study/studies and/or contemporary business issues | Communicates using some business terminology and concepts
1–4 marks: Makes limited reference to human resource strategies and/or effective human resource management | May identify case study/studies | Uses basic business terminology


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Strategies in human resource management
• Leadership style
• Job design – general or specific tasks
• Recruitment – internal or external, general or specific skills
• Training and development – current or future skills
• Performance management – developmental or administrative
• Rewards – monetary and non-monetary, individual or group, performance pay
• Global – costs, skills, supply
• Workplace disputes
– resolution – negotiation, mediation, grievance procedures, involvement of courts and tribunals
Effectiveness of human resource management
• Indicators
– corporate culture
– benchmarking key variables
– changes in staff turnover
– absenteeism
– accidents
– levels of disputation
– worker satisfaction.


WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: choose the correct indicators and strategies
Better responses: provide a variety of detailed indicators that link well with the selected strategies
Better responses: provide depth of knowledge specific for each strategy using sub-points to expand, for example, internal versus external recruitment; details on how a grievance procedure can assist in workplace disputes
Better responses: make clear links between the indicator and the strategy
Better responses: make a clear judgement of the relationship between the strategies and indicators through the case study
Better responses: draw out both the positive and negative relationships between the strategies and the indicators
Better responses: demonstrate sustained judgement of each indicator throughout the response
Better responses: move beyond the indicator as the criteria of their evaluation and consider the other positive/negative impacts of implementing the strategy
Better responses: investigate more than one strategy that could be used to improve an indicator, or how one strategy could improve a number of indicators.
To improve: making specific judgements/criteria when evaluating, rather than just saying a strategy is effective. For example, the positive or negative impacts of using a strategy
To improve: incorporating and applying case studies into their response rather than using them as a sentence at the end of a paragraph
To improve: providing the why and the how of the relationship between strategies and indicators
To improve: including sufficient depth to demonstrate an understanding of the strategies/indicators.

STUDENT RESPONSE:

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-20>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '17–20'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a 6 to 8 line plan of what a full-mark response would cover, one line per paragraph, not a full essay>"}
